name: security-gitlab-ci-protected-context-review
intent: GitLab CI source trust and protected variable/runner exposure
artifacts: Pipeline sources, merge-request/fork context, protected refs/variables, includes and runner selection.
trace: Trace lower-trust YAML/code/includes into jobs that receive protected material or trusted runner access. Preserve the exact event/ref permission context.
experiment: Use an isolated pipeline fixture with a synthetic secret marker and inert job; compare trusted ref and lower-trust merge-request configuration.
disproof: A variable name or protected runner tag is not material access if the pipeline policy withholds it.
repair: Bind protected context to trusted source/includes and retest legitimate releases without leaking real secrets.
branch_decisions: Resolve project/fork identity, pipeline source, branch/tag protection and the actual conditions for protected variables and runners. Masking only changes display behavior; it does not prevent a running script from using a value. A rejected fork pipeline before secret-bearing execution is an effective boundary for that case, not proof of exposure.
operational_method: Distinguish a fork-project pipeline from a parent-project pipeline executing configuration from a fork merge request. Retain project IDs, pipeline source, protected refs/runners and the installed-version protected-resource access settings. A fork pipeline rejected before secret admission is a denial; parent execution using untrusted fork configuration requires a separate source-to-secret-bearing-job trace. Masked output alone is not proof that the running job cannot use the secret.
